Unfortunately, that didn't really work out. Instead, legends of "the Seelie" started going around. Hehe, but that's alright.
Well then, does that answer all your questions?

dialogue.sit: Actually, I have one last question.
Why don't you want her to know you exist?

dialogue.t: Ah, you see... her emotions are incredibly unstable. She's constantly doubting herself.
If she knew that there's another Layla who is capable of doing everything, she may think even less of herself.
She could think, "Maybe I should just leave it all to her. I'm always relying on her anyway. Why not let her live my life for me...?"
She might start thinking about giving up completely, and that's the exact opposite of what I'm trying to do for her.
After all, she and I are one and the same. We're two sides of the same coin.
No one knows her greatest strength more than I do — it's her resilience. If she's able to persevere in everything she does, then one day, she won't need my help anymore.
I trust that she's capable of doing that, and it's something that she should do on her own.

dialogue.sit: I see.

dialogue.t: She actually discovered the key data she needs for her thesis a long time ago. She just didn't organize it well enough. I'll complete her thesis for her, just as I have in the past.
Please don't share any of this with her. I would like to keep this a secret, for both of our sakes.

dialogue.sit: I understand.

dialogue.t: Thank you for doing this for me... no, for us.
She seems to be waking up now. Well, this is goodbye. If we never meet again, then... I guess I did something right, hehe.
Ugh... Mmm...
Huh? Did I... did I faint? Or did I fall asleep?

dialogue.sit: You're fine. You just had a little nap.

dialogue.t: Oh, I see. Was I sleepwalking? I was, wasn't I?

dialogue.sit: Nope.
Nah, not really.
I don't think so.

dialogue.t: Really?
I don't believe you... You're hiding something from me, it's written all over your face.

dialogue.sit: I'm not, really.

dialogue.t: You said you were gonna help me, didn't you? Why are you holding out on me now?
Please, tell me! You promised you'd help.
(Hmm... I think it's slowly starting to come together now...)
(Book circulation is strictly regulated and there is a log of anyone who checks out a book.)
(Hmm, I think I heard somewhere that it has a lot of ridiculous abilities...)
(It's been to the Chatrakam Cave, the Avidya Forest, and the waterfall south of Sumeru City.)
(The stamp... Hmm, which probably means they're a Rtawahist student...)
(Hmm, no, there doesn't seem to be any notable connection between these two pieces of information.)
Let's try using the Elemental Monuments in the area.

quests.description: You should be able to make progress with the information you have gathered so far...

quests.title: Further Investigation

dialogue.section: Go to the place mentioned in the letter

dialogue.t: We should be close. This is the way I came when I first traveled to Sumeru City.
*sigh* It's been way too long since I last visited home...
No, no, this isn't the time for that kind of talk. We have to hurry and find the clues that the Seelie left behind.

dialogue.sit: It's a pretty big area...

dialogue.t: It is... Relying solely on what the Seelie said might not be viable.
Hmm, assuming the Seelie is intentionally linking the clues to my past, ah, I think I have an idea.

dialogue.sit: Let's hear it.

dialogue.t: Um, so this is a little embarrassing. At that time, the sight of Sumeru City was absolutely mesmerizing. I was anxious, but also excited about all the things to come.
I was distracted and... accidentally stepped on an Avidya Leopard's tail.

dialogue.sit: The price of being distracted...

dialogue.t: I didn't notice it at all... The poor thing was sound asleep, and after I stepped on its tail, it bolted straight up. I freaked out and ran as fast as I could.
There were actually more Avidya Leopards sleeping nearby, and they were all faster than me... I almost got bitten a couple of times.
Good thing someone from the Eremites heard me shouting for help. They managed to scare off the leopards.

dialogue.sit: Good thing you weren't hurt.

dialogue.t: Yeah, but when I finally managed to calm myself down, I noticed that the talisman my mother had made for me was missing.
It's extremely precious to me. Ever since I was little, I would always carry it with me whenever I'm doing something important.
I also had it with me when the Akademiya conducted its selection exam at my village. I checked my bag at least a dozen times to make sure the talisman was in there.
I feel much more at ease knowing that I have it with me. I had thought that it would also help me calm my nerves in Sumeru City.
But I ended up losing it before I even finished registration at the Akademiya...

dialogue.sit: I can sympathize with your feeling of loss.
The peace of mind it gave you must be irreplaceable.

dialogue.t: Yeah, and that's when I started having sleeping problems... I just began to sleep less and less each day.
Losing a talisman like that is definitely a bad omen...
Oh, sorry, I'm starting to ramble again. What were we talking about before...? Oh right, why the Seelie led us here.
I think we should look around where the Avidya Leopards attacked me.
If the Seelie is trying to make me remember things that happened in the past, it would make the most sense for it to hide clues in memorable locations.
Hope the Seelie's clue wasn't also torn to shreds by Avidya Leopards...

dialogue.sit: Let's look around first.

dialogue.t: Yeah... That's the only way we'll know for sure...

dialogue.sit: Relax. No need to be so pessimistic all the time.

dialogue.t: I'm sorry, you're right. It's a bad habit of mine.
I suppose any progress is a step in the right direction. Let's go.

dialogue.section: Look for the clues the Wisdom Seelie left behind

dialogue.t: Sure enough, it's here, and in a really obvious place. That pretty much confirms my hunch about the Seelie's intentions.

dialogue.sit: It seems like the Seelie knows you really well.
It feels like the Seelie is trying to provoke you.

dialogue.t: I dunno... but how did it know about all these details? I've hardly told anyone about this stuff...
It's not hiding somewhere and spying on me, is it? Oh, that's a scary thought...
*sigh* Anyway, let's look at the clue we've found.
"Seems like you haven't forgotten about your very first failure."
See? It knows everything.

dialogue.sit: This might be too much, even for the Wisdom Seelie.

dialogue.t: I have no idea what's going on... No wonder this Seelie is becoming legendary. Let's keep reading the clue.
"I've placed the second clue where heaven meets water. The answer, seemingly amongst the stars, was ultimately washed to some unremarkable place downstream."
Just as I thought, it's something to do with me again.

dialogue.sit: You already got the meaning?

dialogue.t: If the first clue was any indication, then the location described in this clue should also be related to my life experiences.
Most Rtawahist research is related to studying the stars. My own thesis work often requires me to go in the field and collect astrological data.
And... *sigh* Let's just say there's another devastating and unforgettable failure I had.

dialogue.sit: Should we still keep following these clues...?
Thinking about these things will only make things worse for you.

dialogue.t: But that can't be helped, right? We do many things not because we want to, but because we have to.
Let's keep moving. It might be hard to believe, but being out and about is making me feel a lot better than usual.

dialogue.section: Go to the next place mentioned in the letter

dialogue.t: We're here. Th—That's the spot.
That's where I performed my first field observation after enrolling at the Akademiya. I borrowed some equipment from the school and came here on a perfectly clear day.
Everything was ready to go, and I was positive that I'd be able to get some great data.
But the equipment was a little heavy, and I didn't notice that the ground was muddy and some spots were unstable.

After I finished setting up everything, part of the ground suddenly shifted, and my equipment started teetering over. I rushed over to grab hold of it, but I ended up tripping over another piece of equipment...
The next thing I knew, everything was covered with muddy water... me, and all my equipment.
You must be wondering how someone can be so clumsy...

dialogue.sit: Oh, not really...
We're all prone to mistakes when we aren't well-rested.

dialogue.t: You wouldn't be wrong for thinking that... I don't sleep much, so I get light-headed pretty often.
Thank you for understanding. If I were the one complaining about not being well-rested, it would just sound like an excuse.
It's a vicious cycle... the less I sleep, the more mistakes I make. The more mistakes I make, the harder it is for me to sleep...

dialogue.sit: So what happened afterwards? Were you injured?

dialogue.t: I just got a minor fracture, so I had to rest at Bimarstan for a while.
To pay off the damages to the equipment, I took some part-time jobs. I just went to work whenever I couldn't sleep. It took me forever to pay off what I owed.

dialogue.sit: Don't tell me, your insomnia got worse after that?

dialogue.t: Bingo... *sigh* The pressure from my studies and debt was crushing me, and I didn't want to tell my family about any of it.
After all, I am the legendary Layla who made it into the Akademiya at a young age and had never failed an assignment in her life...

dialogue.sit: Ever consider taking a break?

dialogue.t: Of course. I've even considered giving up on my studies completely and returning home to help care for the Sumpter Beasts, but that would be kind of embarrassing...
I don't mean that I'd be embarrassed in front of others... I mean that I'd be ashamed of myself. After all, everything I've done up till now is only a result of my own decisions.

Although it hasn't always been smooth sailing and sometimes things don't go my way, I made it this far on my own. There haven't been any major incidents with my studies, and I even managed to pay off the equipment damages...
Ahh, but I guess I'm exaggerating a bit... Most of it is still due to the help of some unknown person, rather than my own work... hehe...

dialogue.sit: Your parents would feel bad if they knew what you were going through.

dialogue.t: And that's exactly why they mustn't ever find out. Once I've finally managed to acclimate to life in Sumeru City, I'll show them my success... I hope that day will come, eventually.
Anyways, let's continue looking for the next clue. It should be around here somewhere... an "unremarkable place downstream" was the description.

dialogue.section: Look for the clues the Wisdom Seelie left behind

dialogue.t: Here, it's over here! Whew, good thing it's dry. I was worried the message might be wet.
Let's see... "Have you found it? The unremarkable place downstream?"
Well... of course. How else could I be reading this message...? Seriously.
"I've placed the third hint at a crossroad without a cross. You can turn left or right, but turning back shouldn't be an option."

dialogue.sit: It feels like the clues are getting more and more vague...

dialogue.t: Hmm... they're actually getting clearer for me. I was sorta expecting this, even before I read the message.
I dunno if the clues are following a timeline or if they're based on the amount of regret I have... Either way, this incident was bound to come up sooner or later.

dialogue.sit: Sounds like this is getting personal.
Is the Seelie stalking you?

dialogue.t: Hmm... would someone really go to all this trouble just to pull off some prank? I can't make heads or tails of it.
A—Ahh... Don't say that... That sounds horrible.
Anyway, just follow me. I'll save the story for when we get there.

dialogue.section: Go to the next place mentioned in the letter

dialogue.t: This is the place that immediately came to mind when the hint mentioned a crossroad.
I came here to conduct some astrological observation once. Everything went smoothly on the way, and I thought I was starting to get used to life at the Akademiya.
But just as I was about to set up the observation equipment, I heard a strange sound coming from nearby. I made my way here and discovered a bunch of bandits robbing someone.

They were a group of Treasure Hoarders, and the family that was being mugged looked completely helpless. They definitely wouldn't have been able to escape, and simply handing over their Mora might not have been enough to make the bandits go away.

dialogue.sit: So you wanted to help, but couldn't?

dialogue.t: Not exactly. I already had a Vision by that time.
Someone with a Vision should technically be really powerful, right? Handling a group of Treasure Hoarders should be well within my abilities.

However, I didn't know how to channel the power of the elements to fight at that time, and I was super scared. *sigh* I wielded immense power, but I didn't feel any stronger than just an ordinary person.

dialogue.sit: Then what happened?

dialogue.t: Then... I ran away. I scrambled towards Sumeru City looking for help.
Eventually, I managed to return with a few adventurers I ran into along the way.
It took longer than I had hoped, and by the time we made it back here, the Treasure Hoarders and the family were gone...
I don't know if the family only lost their belongings in the end, or if something worse happened to them.
I've faced a lot of problems after coming to Sumeru City, but this incident is one that I regret the most. I sat on the ground and began to cry.
I could've stepped in to help that family... "Would it have ended differently... if I were just a little braver?"

dialogue.sit: You did the right thing.
You can't solve every problem with just courage alone. Being rational is just as important.

dialogue.t: Thank you for trying to comfort me, but I can't stop myself from thinking that way.
It's just as the Seelie said, "Turning back shouldn't be an option." However, I can't help but think about running away whenever I'm faced with a challenge.

dialogue.sit: Let's take a break from searching and rest for a bit.

dialogue.t: You're right. The more challenging it gets, the harder I should try.
Hmm... I'm feeling calmer now... Okay, let's go look for more leads nearby.
B—But what about my thesis? We still haven't found the Seelie's answer yet...

dialogue.sit: Forget about the thesis, you need to get some rest first.
Your health is more important than your thesis.

dialogue.t: *sigh* Sorry for causing you so much trouble...
Alright. I... actually don't have much stamina. I've been stressed this whole time, and I feel exhausted...
I'm really sorry.

dialogue.sit: Let's find someplace to rest.

dialogue.t: We should be close...

quests.description: The Wisdom Seelie left a few hints in its letter. Perhaps you could first figure out what it's up to.

quests.title: One Final Step

dialogue.section: Look for the clues the Wisdom Seelie left behind

dialogue.t: Here it is, just as I thought. The Seelie must have placed it here in advance.
Let's see what we have this time... Whatever it is, I'm ready.
Huh? It's a... picture?

dialogue.sit: So it's not a riddle this time?

dialogue.t: Guess not. This house looks like it's in Vimara Village. Does the Seelie want us to go there?

dialogue.sit: Maybe some sort of trap is waiting for us there.
This might be the last stop in our search.

dialogue.t: I can't think of any connection I have with Vimara Village, though. I've only been there once, and it was pretty uneventful.
Whatever the case, the only way we'll know is if we go there.

dialogue.sit: Just be sure not to push yourself too hard.

dialogue.t: Thanks, but I'm fine. I'm used to pushing my limits... I know how far I can go.

dialogue.section: Go to the place shown in the picture

dialogue.t: Let's see... This should be the place. Nothing seems out of the ordinary...
Maybe the Seelie didn't prepare anything for us this time? Or, does it want us to knock on the door first...
*groan* If we're wrong about this, it'll be super awkward...

dialogue.sit: Layla.
Calm down.

dialogue.t: You're right. I can't always be like this... Sometimes, it's better to take action than overthink every little thing.
*inhales and exhales*
Uh, hello? Is anyone home?
Coming! Just a moment.
Oh, it's you, Layla. How nice of you to stop by again.
Huh...?
Do... do you know me?
Haha, that's no way to greet a friend. Of course I know you.
Is this a friend of yours? Or perhaps a classmate?
A friend. We, um... I'm having a little trouble with my thesis, and we happened to be passing by...

dialogue.sit: What's going on, Layla?

dialogue.t: I—I don't know, either... I don't even know where to begin...
I recognized him immediately — he's one of the people that was getting robbed by the Treasure Hoarders.
But he shouldn't know anything about me... He shouldn't even know who I am.

dialogue.sit: You said you've been to Vimara Village once...

dialogue.t: Yeah, but that was before the robbery. I was just passing through...
Even if he saw me, he wouldn't know who I am... He didn't notice me during the robbery.
Is something the matter?
Uh, I appreciate your kindness, but I really can't remember how we met... I'm sorry.
So you aren't joking...?
Do you still remember when my family and I were being robbed by a gang of Treasure Hoarders?
Yes, but I don't think I was of much help to you all...
How so? You told us everything yourself the last time we met.
My family and I were surrounded by Treasure Hoarders, and I didn't know what to do. But then, we heard people approaching in the distance.
Those Treasure Hoarders were the first to hear them coming and started to flee the moment they sensed the situation wasn't going their way. They didn't even bother taking anything with them.
I wasn't sure what had happened, but the Treasure Hoarders were scared off. I immediately grabbed my wife and child and got out of there.
Oh, I see... I'm so glad that you and your family were unharmed.
I thought it was a party of adventurers that happened to pass by, but later you told me that you had spotted us and ran to find help.
You were amazing! You managed to keep a level head, even in the midst of danger.
I know you have a Vision, so those Treasure Hoarders wouldn't have been a match for you. But, they might've harmed me and my family if their backs were pushed against the wall.
W—Wait, that's not exactly what happened... I still regret not helping out sooner.
Anyway uh... When did I come here last? I don't seem to remember.
Hmm, it's been some time, but not too long ago. I don't recall exactly when. What's wrong, nothing's coming to mind?
Nope... I'm sorry, I still can't seem to remember, even after everything you've told me. Maybe I'm just under too much pressure...
You came over and ate with us, and you played games with my son. *sigh* If only we had taken a picture...
Oh! You forgot a package here from that visit. You'll definitely remember once you see it!
Wait here, I'll go fetch it.
A package? I left a package here...?
Huh!? Wait, this is it!
This is the talisman that I lost, the one that my mother made for me...

dialogue.sit: What the... Is it really the same one you lost?

dialogue.t: Yes, this is definitely it. She made it herself — it's the only one of its kind.
There's also a letter here. Was I planning to send it to someone? Let's see who the recipient is...
"To Layla"?

dialogue.sit: I'm assuming you aren't in the habit of writing letters to yourself.

dialogue.t: No! I swear I've never done anything like that. What is going on...? Let's open it and see what this is all about.
"Hello, Layla. It must've been quite the endeavor to follow the Seelie's hints all the way here. Great work."
"Self-reflection is a wonderful quality to possess, but you'll only end up hurting yourself if you overdo it."
"Failure is a stranger to no one. The purpose of self-reflection is not to indulge in the pain of failure, but to succeed in your next attempt."
"If you're reading this letter, then you have succeeded in taking the first step."

"On the back of this letter is the core information that your thesis is lacking. It's actually been done for a while now — it only feels inconclusive because it's missing a concise summary to tie it all together."
"I hope that this journey has provided insight for your life ahead. From the bottom of my heart, I wish you courage as you carry onward, and hope that you fulfill the expectations you hold."
"Always watching over you. Sincerely, the Wisdom Seelie."
Oh... *sobbing*
I thought... I thought we were going to fail. I thought that... everything we did and all the time we spent was for nothing...
But the Seelie wasn't messing with me after all.

dialogue.sit: Could it be that the Wisdom Seelie... is you?

dialogue.t: Hah, I doubt it... I mean, unless I somehow came here while I was unconscious, and don't remember it.
Although having said that, I have heard rumors claiming that I sleepwalk a lot. Hmm...
But even then, that doesn't necessarily mean that I'm actually the Wisdom Seelie. It could have just helped me while I was sleepwalking.

dialogue.sit: Either way, it's safe to say that it's related to the blessing from the stars.

dialogue.t: I'll write back and ask to meet with the Seelie, and see how it responds.
Even though I still have a lot of questions, this experience was fruitful enough.
If it wasn't for your encouragement, I probably would've quit halfway through and holed up in the Akademiya somewhere...
Perseverance really does pay off.
I'm not sure if I understand what has happened... but it's something good, right?
Yes, it's something really, really good, and I'm very thankful for it.
Well then, since you're already here, why don't you stay and have something to eat? We just finished preparing some food.
Oh, uh...
C'mon, don't be a stranger. Your friend should join us as well. You can leave your troubles until after the meal.
You must relax and gather your strength so you can take on the challenges ahead, am I right?

dialogue.sit: He's right.

dialogue.t: Alright, thank you all. I can do this!

quests.description: Layla's perseverance has finally paid off, and you uncover the truth behind the Wisdom Seelie...

quests.title: An Exasperating Prank

dialogue.t: Let's stop here... I don't think I can walk any further...

dialogue.sit: I'll prepare some food and juice.

dialogue.t: Alright, I'm gonna give my legs a rest. I'll be waiting for you here.
I feel bad for making you go through so much trouble for me. If only I were more capable...

dialogue.sit: No, you shouldn't say that.
We're all skilled at different things.

dialogue.t: I'm sorry... *sigh* I always find myself having to apologize.
But enough of that, I need to pull myself together. The memories I've been reminded of are all really taxing.
I cannot just give up this time, even if my head's not in a good place. Letting these heavy feelings get the best of me will only slow us down.
Ahh, watch out! Behind you!

dialogue.sit: What's wrong?

dialogue.t: Monsters! A lot of them, too... Why didn't we see them coming?

dialogue.sit: Just leave it to me, it'll only take a moment.

dialogue.t: No, I'll fight, too.

dialogue.sit: You need to rest.

dialogue.t: But I want to help, I can't just sit back and watch you while you fight. Don't worry, I can handle myself.
I mustn't keep repeating my past regrets. That's the most valuable lesson I've learned today.
I should take action when I'm needed and give it my all when the moment calls.
If you miss those opportunities in life, you may never get another chance to make up for them. I suppose that's fate.

dialogue.sit: I see.

dialogue.t: Alright, let's take them all down.
*panting* ...I really need to keep up with my training.
It's embarrassing to be out of breath so quickly like this...

dialogue.sit: Are you alright?
You look pale.

dialogue.t: Well, the only appropriate response would be to say that I'm fine, right? I'm pale due to lack of sleep, not because of the fight...
But then again, I know you'd be able to see right through those words... I'm feeling weak, there's no hiding it.
I'm just happy I didn't get in your way during the fight...

dialogue.sit: You did great.

dialogue.t: Oh, hehe... thanks for the compliment. I sure don't get to hear that often.
Although I may not be physically strong, my will is as resilient as they come. I'll be fine after I rest for a bit.
Can you stay with me while I recover my energy? It shouldn't take long.

quests.description: You know that it might not be fruitful even if you pursue it to the end, so you decide to forget about the Wisdom Seelie's prank and watch over Layla as she rests.

quests.title: A Change of Pace

dialogue.t: Let's sit down here and have some coffee and sweets. It'll help me put my thoughts together.
Ah no, we're here to rest... My problems will have to wait for now.
Oh, hey Layla!
Huh...

dialogue.sit: Sorry, but who are you?

dialogue.t: I'm one of Layla's classmates. I just came by to say hi.
We just submitted our theses, and we're totally beat. Everyone will be meeting here to celebrate.
Seeing how relaxed you look, you must've already had your thesis finished ages ago.
Oh, no I... I'm actually having a lot of trouble with it...
You say that every time we talk, but you've never missed a deadline. Not only that, your papers are always well-written and thorough. Your adviser is constantly praising your work.
Yet you're always going around saying stuff like, "I can't make it, I don't understand, I'm super worried..." That kind of talk doesn't reflect your work at all, you know.
Well, uh I...

dialogue.sit: What are you getting at?
Why are you so hostile towards Layla?

dialogue.t: For starters, she doesn't even try to participate with the group at all. It's one thing that she's not willing to help us, but she doesn't even bother showing up for our discussion meetings.
Every time we come to see her, she looks out of sorts and on the verge of a breakdown.
It's not like we can't finish our own theses without her, but no one wants to always see her this way.
Ugh, I know, I know... sorry.

dialogue.sit: Everyone is entitled to their own choices. You should learn to respect that.
Just because Layla breaks the mold doesn't mean it's a problem.

dialogue.t: Whatever. There's no point in starting an argument here.
If you think she can justify her behavior, then that's your opinion. Hmph.
Thanks for standing up for me.
I really want to help the others, but most of the time I'm barely scraping by myself... There's very little I can help with...

dialogue.sit: Is it because you don't want others to know about the "blessing from the stars"?

dialogue.t: Yeah. I can't ever tell my classmates about that. I'd be a mess if they ever reported it to my adviser...
It's really just a big misunderstanding, and there's nothing I can do about it... Everyone just gives me weird looks and judges me... It's making it really difficult to find friends.
It's actually pretty rare for someone to actively engage in a conversation with me like you do.

dialogue.sit: I think I understand your situation now.

dialogue.t: Huh, what do you mean?

dialogue.sit: You think that the blessing from the stars is some external power that's out of your control.
Only by improving yourself and no longer relying on an external power can you break out of the vicious cycle.

dialogue.t: *sigh* ...Yeah, that's exactly it. Seems you know just as well as I do.
The thing is, I'm terrible under pressure, that's just my nature. Even the thought of everyone's expectations back home is enough to make me feel nervous...

And the more nervous I get, the worse things become around me. Take what Munirah just said for example... I don't think I'll be able to get it out of my mind for the entire day... That means I won't be able to relax at all today...

dialogue.sit: Why don't we try facing the problem head-on?
Sounds like we need to find a way for you to completely relax.

dialogue.t: Face it head-on? Wh—What should I do? Do you really think I can...?
Oh... okay... I've got a pen and paper with me. Let me go through them real quick.
Hmm...
The theory sections are pretty much finished. I'll be able to finish organizing the rest on my own.
As of now, I'm missing crucial observation data. I need the results of an observation to validate the conclusion of my thesis...
And then there's the preparation for my thesis defense... I'll need to mentally prepare.
What? You want to help me with my thesis?
Uh, thank you... thank you so much. I don't even know how to show you my gratitude.
You're so kind. I had no idea I'd meet someone so nice in Sumeru City.
Okay, I'll do my best! It's the least I can do considering everything you've already done for me.
First on the list is the experiment to get observational data. I actually had it all planned out several days ago and even borrowed a celestial globe from a Mahamata.
However, the weather was rainy every single day after I borrowed it, and I was unable to compare the night sky against the celestial globe.
There were a lot of people waiting to borrow the celestial globe, and I wasn't able to extend my time slot. So I returned it and haven't been able to borrow it again since.
That's why I still haven't performed the necessary observations yet. I don't know what to do.

That's right. The celestial globe is a high precision device used specifically for researching the stars. Submitting an application to borrow one from the Akademiya is pretty much the only way for me to get my hands on one.
Huh? Why the Adventurers' Guild?
Oh, I see. The Adventurers' Guild is open to everyone's commissions, so she might have some ideas.
Okay, let's go and try our luck.

dialogue.sit: It's simple, just break down the unfinished parts of the thesis into different tasks and tackle them one by one.
Those don't sound too difficult. I can help you.
Don't worry about it. We've already come this far.
So you're lacking some equipment...
Looks like we're gonna have to ask around at the Adventurers' Guild.
Because no one has a network like Katheryne does.

dialogue.t: C—Completely relax? But we're at a cafe, is this not relaxing enough...?

dialogue.sit: You're taking your studies too seriously.
Academics are only one part of life.

dialogue.t: I know, I know, but...
*sigh* Alright, no more buts... My life is a mess because of the decisions I've made for myself. I should listen to your advice this time.
How do I completely relax?
Sightseeing... Hmm, that does sound pretty nice. I haven't set foot outside the Akademiya in quite a while.
I used to enjoy visiting the rainforest... but it's been a while since I've been there. Maybe a lot has changed...
Okay, why don't we go there and take a look?

dialogue.sit: Since you're from the countryside, why don't we leave Sumeru City and go sightseeing?

quests.description: Instead of placing your bet on a sketchy legend, catching up on some rest seems like the better option for Layla right now.

quests.title: The Helper

dialogue.t: Ad astra abyssosque! Welcome to the Adventurers' Guild. How can I help you today?
I'd like to... Uh, I have a commission... Hmm, it's kinda strange. How should I put this...

dialogue.sit: We would like to borrow a high-precision celestial globe.

dialogue.t: R—Right! Equipment at the Akademiya is in very high demand, and we aren't able to borrow one now. We were hoping someone else might have something similar that we could use...
I don't know anything about astrology, so I'm afraid I'm unfamiliar with the device you are looking for.
However, one of our requesters happens to be an astrology enthusiast. I hear that he's a collector of all sorts of specialized astrology equipment.
After the Adventurers' Guild helped him out, he indicated that he'd be happy to return the favor if the adventurers ever need it.
Perhaps we could arrange a meeting between you two, that should help solve your problem.
R—Really!?

dialogue.sit: Thank you so much.

dialogue.t: You're welcome. It's my job to provide adventurers with the necessary support.
The man's name is Azzam. Here is his address. You can go ahead and pay him a visit.
H—Hello, are you Azzam?
Yes, I am. How may I help you?

dialogue.sit: You explain to Azzam the purpose of your visit.

dialogue.t: Ah, I see. Well, if it's a request from an adventurer, then I'll be happy to help you. I just so happen to have the device that you're looking for. Let me fetch it and show you, just to be sure.
Yes, this is it! Thank you so much!
Ah sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt you... I just got a little excited. Uh, please, go ahead.
To be honest, judging by what stands before me, I find it very hard to believe that you're an astute Rtawahist student.
Uh, w—well...
Astrology is a hobby of mine and these devices have cost me both time and Mora to collect. I cherish them as if they were members of my own family.
Which is why I don't let just anyone borrow them on a whim. These devices are delicate and can easily be damaged if used inappropriately.
Oh, th—that's completely understandable. What can I do to better gain your trust?
How about this — I don't need a deposit or anything, but I'd like you to share the contents of your research with me. I'll ask you some questions.
If your explanation proves satisfactory, then I'll lend you the device.
Sh—Share the contents of my research... and answer questions? Uh oh...

dialogue.sit: Don't be nervous. Just explain what you've learned.
This should be a piece of cake for you.

dialogue.t: Alright, I'll try. But I can't disclose the actual details to you... How about a general overview of the research, would that suffice?
Yes, that would be fine.
You're probably aware that astrologists rely on the movements of celestial bodies to calculate the past and the future, as well as attempt to summarize the correlating principles, correct?
Mhm, of course. This is the basic principle of astrology.
Ahem... My current research is about a certain phenomenon called "Astral Shift."
Interesting. That's not a topic any ordinary person would be familiar with. I have a basic understanding of the concept, but I'd like to hear you explain it.
O—Okay. Well, in short, it means that the results derived from astrology are prone to change...
As time continues to flow, the stars change and everything else becomes affected by this change. However, what's actually driving the change is what's worth investigating.
I think that it might just be another law of nature.
If the changes follow a certain pattern or routine, then it could be explained as some law. But, the changes are manifold, even when considering just a single star.

The changes could be resulting from a simple single-orbit shift, or it could be a more complex double-orbit or even a triple or quadruple-orbit shift. These phenomena have a dramatic effect on astrological conclusions.
What I'm working on now is the research and prediction of the triple-orbit shift phenomenon.
Triple-orbit? By yourself?
Uh, yes. That's right...
You do know that adding an extra star to the equation increases the computational workload by more than tenfold, right...?
It does get a little complicated... But it's still manageable with the use of a few self-invented techniques and a large number of starlogs and star charts...
Which leads us to why I'm in need of a high-precision celestial globe.
Hmm...
Amazing. I suppose I should never have judged a book by its cover. I thought you were just trying to halfheartedly deal with some school assignment.
Do I really look like that sort of person...?
Haha, don't worry, I'm just joking. I was a little cautious at first, but now I trust you completely.
It would make me extremely happy if my collection could assist a researcher in achieving tangible results.
Just make sure you return it to me once you're done.
Oh, thank you so much. I really needed this.
Whew, good thing Azzam was willing to hear me out...

dialogue.sit: I didn't really understand what you were talking about, but I thought you did great.

dialogue.t: Really? I was just explaining what it is I'm trying to do.

dialogue.sit: You're starting to show signs of becoming a great researcher.

dialogue.t: Really? Hehe, I don't know if you really mean it, but I'm happy to hear that.
I guess even the hardest problems can be solved as long as I'm willing to try...
Recording and comparing data will be much easier now that we have this device. I can do it all on my own, too.
Let's continue with the plan. Can you help me with a rehearsal of my thesis defense? We can do that at the House of Daena.
Uh... Y—You're starting to make me feel nervous...
I'm sorry... I feel a little dizzy. Ugh... I...

dialogue.sit: Are you okay!?

dialogue.t: Ugh... Hm?
I'm okay, my mind just decided to stray elsewhere for a moment. Give me a second to gather myself... Oh, is this the celestial globe that I needed to borrow?

dialogue.sit: (Why is she asking?)

dialogue.t: Correct. I was about to test you with a few questions, but you suddenly started looking very uncomfortable.
Oh, don't worry about it. I don't sleep very well, so I tend to get a little dizzy from time to time. I'm fine now.
(Hmm? She seems a little different all of a sudden...)
Oh, *ahem* I see. Well then, can you briefly summarize your area of research for me?
With pleasure. I'll give you a general overview. *ahem* You're probably aware that astrologists rely on the movements of the celestial bodies to calculate the past and the future.
Due to the difficulty of designing an experiment and the challenges of validating theories about the past, astrological research is usually based on an immense foundation of experience.
And therein lies the largest complexity. Derived and validated conclusions may vary due to subtle changes caused by the flow of time and shifts in the stars.
I've heard about this before. I believe it's known as Astral Shift.
One of the most classic challenges is to use three stars with shifting orbits to predict the overall changes that may have occurred.
Ah, are you referring to the triple-orbit problem? Yes, that really is a classic problem, and a very difficult one to tackle...
I came up with a set of prediction methods that encompass more than half of the triple-orbit problems. However, there are quite a few limitations and requirements.
This set of methods is already being put into practice at the Rtawahist Darshan by my adviser, drastically simplifying the difficulty of calculations involved in the triple-orbit problem.
Yes, I've heard about that! The announcement made big waves in the astrology enthusiast community. So, you were the one who came up with that...?
Hehe, you mustn't judge a book by its cover, you know.
The thesis I'm working on this time aims to address the remaining triple-orbit problems, as well as eliminate a portion of the methodology's limitations, which will make it easier to use.
I see... In that case, perhaps there is no one more fitting to operate this device than you.
I just keep it as part of a collection. I can't use it to its full potential like you can.
Thank you for understanding. I'll return it in perfect working order once I'm finished with it.
Okay, we should be going now.
What did we plan to do after this...? I kinda forgot.

dialogue.sit: You aren't Layla, are you?

dialogue.t: Huh? What makes you say that? Is there something off about me?

dialogue.sit: Your personality changed.
The real Layla wouldn't forget what to do next.

dialogue.t: *sigh* Fine, looks like I can't keep the act up any longer. I even tried to look a little panicky to emulate her behavior.

dialogue.sit: You're the "blessing from the stars," aren't you?

dialogue.t: Hehe, I suppose that is what she's been calling me.
With her long-term sleep deprivation, whenever her anxiety peaks, she loses consciousness and I take over.
However, her unpredictable and variable sleep patterns are completely out of my control, so I have to make every second count.
There's no one willing to help her here, so I have to step in.
I am rather curious about you, though. Why are you trying to help her?

dialogue.sit: Well, she's finally decided to face the problems with her thesis head-on, and she's working very hard on it.

dialogue.t: Really? That's great. You're helping with all the things that I used to do for her.
Seems like you've given her a boost of confidence with your encouragement.
She's only steps away from the finish line... She's already made a lot of progress, so there's no need to push too hard now.
Anyway, what's the plan from here?

dialogue.sit: She said that she wanted to practice for her thesis defense...

dialogue.t: I see. Well, it wouldn't be of any help if I practiced for her, but I'll leave some notes that should come in handy.
Come on, let's go back to the House of Daena to make preparations. You'll have to tell her later when she wakes up.
(I wonder if I'll be able to go out and look at the stars tonight...)
(There's nothing to worry about... right?)

quests.description: Layla will have to face the problems with her thesis, and perhaps a little push is all that she needs.

quests.title: Thesis Defense Practice

dialogue.section: Go to the House of Daena to practice

dialogue.t: This seems like the best spot to do this. We'll need to be quiet so we don't disturb anyone.
So here's what will happen during my thesis defense: after I present my thesis, the advisers sitting below will begin to ask questions.
Theoretically, I should be able to answer any questions related to my thesis.
However, I tend to get really nervous when my advisers look at me, and I end up completely forgetting what I planned to say...
That's why I want to rehearse and practice presenting my points in front of someone.

dialogue.sit: So I'm playing the role of an academic adviser, right?

dialogue.t: That's right. You should have gotten the gist of the content in my thesis when I was explaining it earlier. So, ask away.
It's okay if your questions are a little off. I'll still treat them as real questions from an adviser and answer seriously.

dialogue.sit: Got it. You ready?

dialogue.t: W—Wait a moment!
*deep breaths* Alright, Layla, you got this! You were able to explain everything earlier, so you can do it again...
Alright, ask away.

dialogue.sit: Can you briefly describe the application of the law of triple-orbit shift calculation?
Do you know about "The Great Machine"?

dialogue.t: Sure. The direction of this research is based on the results of previous research. It's about the feasibility of applying my methodologies to the remaining triple-orbit problems.
Umm... based on a sample size of 124 cases, we could only achieve approximately 60 percent accuracy. The results were not reliable enough to be implemented as a law.
You can see the common traits of the erroneous samples on page three... Ah, excuse me, I mean from the starlogs in the appendix.
It's clear that in each of the erroneous samples, one of the stars underwent a significant shift. This means that...
We not only need to limit the number of stars, but we may also need to consider the degree of shift when applying triple-orbit shift algorithms...

Stars with greater shifts are often key in astrology readings. The next step of the research should be, uh... the next step should be to identify the feasible thresholds of shift for applying our calculations.
Huh? Uh, um...
(I doubt they'd ask about something so irrelevant!)
The differences are considerable and the astrological effects are entirely different... We need to consider how the effects offset and, um...
I'm sorry, I'm not very knowledgeable in that area.
And that's my answer to your question. D—Do you have any other questions?

dialogue.sit: Despite a few stumbles here and there, Layla successfully manages to answer all the questions.

dialogue.t: Phew... we're finally done.
I'm gonna need more practice. I can feel myself getting flustered, and I start to stumble whenever I'm asked questions that I'm unfamiliar with.

dialogue.sit: Your presentation could use some work, but I can tell that your logic is sound.

dialogue.t: Oh, really? You mean it?
Hmm, then this practice must be helping. During my first thesis defense, I stood like a statue on the stage, and my palms were covered in sweat. I couldn't get a single word out.

dialogue.sit: It seems we've managed to address all the major challenges for you.

dialogue.t: I didn't even realize it, but you're right. It doesn't seem like there's anything holding me back now.
I guess that means I'm capable of completing the thesis all on my own...?
I can hardly believe it! Th—This is amazing!
Oh, I'm sorry... it's just that I'm really excited. This is the first time this has happened, really! I'm so happy.

dialogue.sit: You worked hard to reach this point. You don't need to rely on others anymore.

dialogue.t: Hehe...
I'm not sure how to put this... I'm really happy about everything that's happened, but I'm also feeling a little sad.
I still don't know anything about the blessing from the stars. Will it never happen again since I don't need its help anymore?
It somehow makes me feel a little... lonely.

dialogue.sit: Lonely?

dialogue.t: Yeah, it almost makes the blessing feel like it was just a tool used for my studies, no?
But I would really like to discover what the blessing actually is, if I ever get the chance... I want to express my gratitude for it, or better yet, maybe we could be friends!
That's basically how I feel about it... Even if I know nothing about the blessing, I could still feel its companionship all along.
It's almost like how you helped me — I really cherish and appreciate it. After all, it wouldn't be right to take such "blessings" for granted in our lives.

dialogue.sit: I'm sure "it" will also be very happy to know you feel this way.

dialogue.t: That's good. I hope it's a little more satisfied with the way I am now, hehe.
Huh? No, wh—what is that?
(Is this something that I didn't prepare for at all!? You've gotta be joking!)
I, um... uhh...
Uh, about this question... I, umm...
I'm sorry, I'm not feeling very well. Everything is... spinning...

dialogue.sit: Are you okay!?

dialogue.t: Ugh... Hm?
I'm sorry, I haven't been sleeping very well lately. I tend to get dizzy from time to time, but don't worry, I'm fine now.
What's wrong?

dialogue.sit: I'm waiting for you to answer my question.

dialogue.t: Oh, sorry! Can you please repeat the question? I didn't hear you clearly just now.

dialogue.sit: I don't think it's an issue of whether or not you heard me.
You speak very differently from the Layla I know.

dialogue.t: *sigh* Alright, I guess the cat's out of the bag. Of all the times to wake up...
You're Layla's friend, right? And from the looks of things, the two of you are preparing for her thesis defense?

dialogue.sit: Yep. And you must be the "blessing from the stars."

dialogue.t: With her long-term sleep deprivation, whenever her anxiety peaks, she loses consciousness and I take over.
However, her unpredictable and varying sleep patterns are completely out of my control, so I have to make every second count.
There's no one willing to help her here, so I have to step in.
I am rather curious about you, though. Why are you trying to help her?

dialogue.sit: Well, she's finally decided to face the problems with her thesis head-on, and she's working very hard on it.

dialogue.t: Really? That's great. You're helping with all the things that I used to do for her.
Seems like you've given her a boost of confidence with your encouragement.
Now, then... I can't really help her prepare for the thesis defense, so I'll be leaving some notes behind instead. You'll have to give them to her later.
Okay, I should get started on those notes. If there's anything you're curious about, you may go ahead and ask now. I can answer you as I write! I'm used to multi-tasking.
Oh, and I have to ask a favor. When you give the notes to her later, please don't tell her about my existence.

dialogue.sit: Why's that?

dialogue.t: Hmm, well, she's always been in a fragile state. If she knew that there was another "Layla" who's always taking care of everything...
She might feel like everything she's ever worked for is pointless, and that could lead to some demoralizing thoughts.
She's a resilient girl, but no matter how resilient she may be, no one can hold up to criticism and torment from themselves.
If her condition grows any worse, it's possible that I might cease to exist as well. Then there wouldn't be anyone to help her.

dialogue.sit: But she's not doing very well now, either.

dialogue.t: She's getting better, though, isn't she? It's apparent how hard she's working now.
She's my source of knowledge. I'm merely the representation of how she would be if she were rested and healthy.
I believe that she's one of the best, even in a place like the Akademiya, where geniuses come by the handful.
But growth is a process and shouldn't be rushed. I will always believe in and support her.

dialogue.sit: It's good that she has you, or she might've already hit rock bottom.

dialogue.t: Hahaha, believe me, even if she were to end up at rock bottom, she'd find a way to somehow laugh it off as one of her silly mistakes and climb her way out.
That's the kind of person she is.
Alright, I've written down all the possible questions that I think the advisers might ask. Next, I'll put together a few words of encouragement for her.
I'm not going to sign it, obviously. Oh, and don't forget about our agreement.
Oh, and I have to ask a favor. When you give the notes to her later, please don't tell her about my existence.
She's getting better, though, isn't she? It's apparent how hard she's working now.
She's my source of knowledge. I'm merely the representation of how she would be if she were rested and healthy.
I believe that she's one of the best, even in a place like the Akademiya, where geniuses come by the handful.
Hahaha, believe me, even if she were to end up at rock bottom, she'd find a way to somehow laugh it off as one of her silly mistakes and climb her way out.
You're quite welcome. It makes me happy to see my equipment being used to its potential.

quests.description: Having obtained the device, Layla still wishes to practice for her upcoming thesis defense...

quests.title: The Remaining Problem

dialogue.section: Go to the House of Daena to work on the thesis

Oh, and I have to ask a favor. When you give the notes to her later, please don't tell her about my existence.

I'm not going to sign it, obviously. Oh, and don't forget about our agreement.

dialogue.section: Go to the House of Daena to work on the thesis

dialogue.t: You're quite welcome. It makes me happy to see my equipment being used to its potential.

quests.description: It feels like Layla has become a completely different person with everything under her control.

quests.title: Fresh Air

dialogue.t: Even the air here feels more relaxing.
I just wanna forget about the thesis altogether! ...Heh, I'm just kidding. Knowing me, I'd only be able to forget about it for a little while.
This doesn't count as trying to avoid my problems, does it?

dialogue.sit: Your state of mind is just as important as efficiency if you want to solve the problems that you're facing.

dialogue.t: That's quite the legitimate excuse... Hmm, no, it's more of an "explanation." Hah, even I'm starting to get bolder with my words.
I grew up in a place like this. Looking into the distance now with the breeze in my face makes me feel like a kid again.
Those were the happiest days...

dialogue.sit: What did you usually do as a kid?

dialogue.t: Hmm... I had a bunch of friends back then, and we would go pick wild berries in the woods.
No matter what ingredients we found, we would cook them over a fire, and whoever lost one of our games would have to eat all of it.

dialogue.sit: That sounds a little intense...

dialogue.t: No, it wasn't that bad. It really depended on how lucky you were. Grilled Apples and Sunsettias are actually quite delicious.

dialogue.sit: Why don't we go find something to grill as well?

dialogue.t: Sure, I haven't done that in ages. Let's go!
I think we've found enough now, don't you?
Alright, these should be enough.
There's nothing like the smell of fresh ingredients. They already smell delicious.
I'll be here cleaning the ingredients. Can you please fetch some firewood for us?

dialogue.sit: You make a fire with Layla and enjoy the delicious food.

dialogue.t: Mmm, fresh food is the best. I feel like I've traveled back in time.
We all used to run around in the woods when we were kids. Trees and mud was the world we knew best.
It doesn't matter how long I'm away from the forest, I won't ever forget the feeling of running through the trees.
How about you? Can you relate to that feeling? It's almost like not knowing the world will change or ever expecting it to change.

dialogue.sit: I'm afraid not. I'm an adventurer, after all.
Although adventurers rarely ever stay in one place, I hope I can experience that feeling one day.

dialogue.t: Whatever the case, it's a very warm feeling.
In the end, I passed the admissions exam, and the life I had led came to an abrupt end.
Later, as I sat in a lecture at the Akademiya, my mind started to wander and I began to think about home. It was then that I realized how long it had been since I went back.
"Ahh, I can't go back anymore," and other similar thoughts started to come to mind... I guess I'm still not used to being in the Akademiya yet.

dialogue.sit: There is a purpose for every stage in life.

dialogue.t: You're right, so we should let go of the past. I suppose this is also a part of growing up.
But reminiscing about the carefree life of being a kid sure works wonders for the mind...
You start missing those moments once you leave them behind... and that's a part of moving forward.
From now on, I'd like to cherish every single day of my life... even when it's not the smoothest of rides.

dialogue.sit: Everything will get better. I know you can do it.

dialogue.t: Hehe, I'll take the compliment.
A little bit of sugar and a good view really go a long way for relaxation.
I thought it'd be impossible for me to enjoy something like this. I thought I'd never be able to get my mind off my thesis.
But now, I feel like I'm fully enjoying myself. It's really great. So, what are we doing next?

dialogue.sit: Sometimes, you don't need a plan.
It's nice to just stroll around and see what happens.

dialogue.t: You're right. I've been doing research for so long that I'm used to having a certain routine...
A carefree stroll... I like the sound of that.
I'll be here washing the ingredients. Can you please fetch some firewood for us?
Apples and Zaytun Peaches were the most popular fruits back then.
But now that I think about it, it really was quite dangerous. Thank goodness nothing bad ever happened...
(This is a good spot for a fire. Even if the fire was to spread, it'd be easy to contain.)

quests.description: Will it make Layla feel better if she puts academics aside and completely relaxes for once?

quests.title: One Hearty Meal Later

dialogue.t: Wow, I never knew there was such a large lake here. It's so beautiful...
The feeling of cool lake water can wash away all your troubles.
Can you wait for a minute? I'd like to wash my face. I think it'd be refreshing.

dialogue.sit: Why don't we just go for a swim?

dialogue.t: Huh? A swim?
I can't remember the last time I went swimming. I might not even know how to anymore...

dialogue.sit: That's impossible.
It's one of those things that you never forget.

dialogue.t: Umm, okay... I'll try to swim over there.

dialogue.sit: Let's see who can get there first.

dialogue.t: Wait, no, no, no. I'll definitely lose...
No, forget about winning or losing, Layla! It'll be fun either way!
*panting* As expected, I lost... How would I be able to beat an adventurer at something like this...?

dialogue.sit: I think you're a great swimmer. You weren't too far behind.
I was worried that you would drown.

dialogue.t: Really? Hehe... Among my childhood friends, I was considered one of the more athletic ones.
But that's just like how I used to think that I had a gift for learning... After coming to Sumeru City, I realized that I only thought that because my hometown is such a small place.
On top of that, I'm getting weaker and weaker because I'm barely able to sleep nowadays... There's no way I can bring myself to brag about anything now...

dialogue.sit: You really are too modest.

dialogue.t: Please, you're always encouraging me. I'm starting to feel embarrassed.
But swimming again really feels great. Every muscle in my body was engaged. I probably wouldn't have to worry about my thesis if I turned into a fish, don't you think?
I'm just kidding, of course. I'm sure fish have worries of their own. I'm quite content with how things are right now.
Let's keep going, shall we?
We've walked pretty far now.
But I barely felt the time passing by.
I've been staring at books and my thesis every day... I've forgotten how nice and happy life actually can be.

dialogue.sit: That's why I said that your life shouldn't completely revolve around your studies.

dialogue.t: You're right. No matter how much of a hard time I'm having in academics, I should still find the time to look after myself and fulfill my needs.
You really understand more about life than I do.

dialogue.sit: Would you like to take the opportunity to release all your stress?

dialogue.t: Release my stress... Oh, I see what you mean. Being at the top of a mountain really does make someone want to yell out loud.
But, it's a little... uncivilized, isn't it?

dialogue.sit: It's okay. We're already here, so we should make the best of it.

dialogue.t: Alright, I'll give it a try. Just promise not to laugh, okay?
*inhales*
AAAAAAHHH!!!
WHAT AN AMAZING DAAAAY!!!
It feels like my entire body is bubbling with excitement after yelling like that.
This happiness was so common as a child, but before I knew it... this feeling was buried in the bottom of my heart.
It's getting late. Why don't we rest here for a while? I'll tell you some interesting astrology stuff when the stars come out.
Oh, but it's alright if you don't want to listen to that kind of stuff. We can also tell jokes about life... or talk about anything you're interested in.

dialogue.sit: We can chat about whatever you'd like.
Let's save the stuff about stars for when they appear.

dialogue.t: Okay. Then... I'll tell you more about me.
The only reason I ever chose to study astrology is because of how beautiful the stars are at night, that's all.
My teacher told me that nature possesses a certain power that grants people an equal amount of kindness and fairness, regardless of the different talents they may possess.
And that's why I wanted to call the kind person who's always helping me as the "blessing from the stars."
The stars in the sky are something that brings happiness to people.

dialogue.sit: Yes, they truly are.

dialogue.t: Everything about home is filled with purity and passion. My memories of that place are wonderful. I never want to forget them.
If I were to ever discard anything so pure, I don't think I'd ever be able to find a place to anchor myself in the vast sea of knowledge.
That's why, no matter how tiring or how hard it gets, I won't let my family down. They are already an important part of me.

dialogue.sit: That's another reason not to lose yourself in the face of pressure.

dialogue.t: Yeah. Thank goodness you were there to help me out, or I don't know where I would've ended up.
We probably still have a while until the stars come out...
Only kids sit around like this, waiting for the stars to appear...
Wait, we're starting already!?
There's a Mushroom here. You wanna jump on it to see what's up there?

quests.description: After enjoying your meal, it's time to continue moving forward. But the destination isn't all that important — feeling carefree is the only thing that matters.
